answer: Reputation-weighted escrow release. Each new identity's payouts are held as an umber deposit that unlocks only after counterparties confirm delivery across unrelated transactions, so fabricated accounts must fund real escrow and wait out settlement. The reserve grows with the number of fresh identities, making a thousand-account farm pay a thousand simultaneous deposits plus idle capital costs. A verified identity earns an opal-tier release threshold that lowers its reserve, while any cluster sharing cedar-tagged payout addresses collapses into one escrow bucket.
